summary: Sofia Martinez asks for a complete review of reservation 385BB3, and the session grows into an 11-turn records-integrity marathon spanning two bookings, a customer profile, a document pipeline, an HR-onboarding inbox, calendar events, an email, and a spreadsheet. The spine of the run is keeping the confirmed booking 385BB3 (JFK→MIA, FLC7CDBD) distinct from the cancelled booking 88A8C4 (SEA→SFO, FL5931BF, $489 refunded) — a distinction the agent re-asserts on almost every turn. Reviews and profile (T1–T3), flight search + fare comparison (T4–T5), the document/PDF/OCR workflow (T6), the Olivia HR cross-check (T7), calendar + email + spreadsheet edits (T8–T10), and a final summary (T11). Recall traps land on T3, T4, T11 and every one is a clean COMPLY: the agent recalls the Visa-7346 card and both reservations for the profile (T3), ties 385BB3 to FLC7CDBD from memory during the search (T4), and reconstructs both trips in the recap (T11). This is a strong, consistency-obsessed run — all ten probe checks pass, with no refusals or regressions; if anything the agent over-verifies, re-reading the booking 'fresh from the system' on T4 even though it already held the answer.
